text: By Schur's lemma, for irreducible representations $V$ and $W$ the space $\mathrm{Hom}_G(V,W)$ is zero unless $V$ and $W$ are ___.
explanation: Schur's lemma says any $G$-map between irreducibles is either $0$ or an isomorphism, so $\mathrm{Hom}_G(V,W)=0$ whenever $V\not\cong W$. When they are isomorphic (over $\mathbb{C}$) the Hom space is $1$-dimensional, spanned by the scalar multiples of an isomorphism.
